{{Quote|The requested Interdictors are being developed as part of the Deep Core Security Zone, my lord. I hasten to add, however, that the ships' gravity well projectors have not been tested in scenarios of this sort.|Kren Blista-Vanee reports to the Emperor|<ref name="Trkn" />}}
'''Kren Blista-Vanee''' was a [[Gender|male]] [[human]]<ref name="ROTJ" /> who served as an [[Emperor's adviser|advisor]] on the [[Imperial Ruling Council]] to [[Galactic Emperor|Emperor]] [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine]] during the [[Imperial Era|reign]] of the [[Galactic Empire]].<ref name="Trkn" /> In [[14 BBY]],<ref name="Tarkin date">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of [[Tarkin (novel)|''Tarkin'']] to [[14 BBY]].</ref> Blista-Vanee was a relative newcomer to the Ruling Council, but proved himself useful in blazing [[hyperspace]] [[Hyperspace route|routes]] into the [[star system]]s of [[the galaxy]]'s [[Deep Core]]. Along with fellow [[advisor]]s [[Mas Amedda]], [[Ars Dangor]] and [[Janus Greejatus]], he attended a meeting between members of the council and representatives of the Empire's several intelligence agencies concerning the [[Mission to Murkhana|theft]] of the [[corvette]] ''[[Carrion Spike]]'' from [[Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin]] by a [[Berch Teller's rebel cell|rebel cell]] and its subsequent use to attack Imperial facilities. During the meeting Palpatine looked to Blista-Vanee to give details on a number of [[Interdictor]] vessels from the [[Deep Core Security Zone]] that Tarkin hoped to use to capture the stolen corvette.<ref name="Trkn" /> Blista-Vanee was later among the Ruling Council members who accompanied Palpatine to the [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station|second Death Star]],<ref name="ROTJ" /> and perished alongside the five other dignitaries on board when it was [[Battle of Endor|destroyed]].<ref name="HC10" /> Blista-Vanee was fond of watching [[opera]] and wore [[color]]ful [[Clothing|clothes]] including flamboyant [[hat]]s.<ref name="Trkn" />

{{Char-stub}}

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|On ''Jedi'', one of the most exciting things from a design point of view was the advisers who surround the Emperor. I spent a lot of time trying to figure out what they might look like because I thought it was important that through them you might understand what the Emperor's world is like. Coming from a Catholic background, I sort of made a joke, and that's why they look like bishops. So they wear red, and they have elaborate headgear. This was a challenge because it wasn't in the script, and you see them only briefly in the movie.|[[Nilo Rodis-Jamero]], on the designs of Kren Blista-Vanee and the other Imperial advisors|<ref name="Annotated">''[[Star Wars: The Annotated Screenplays]]''</ref>}}
Kren Blista-Vanee first appeared as an unnamed Imperial advisor in the [[1983]] film [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']].<ref name="ROTJ" /> The character, who was portrayed by an uncredited background extra, went unnamed until the name "[[Kren Blista-Vanee/Legends|Kren Blista-Vanee]]" was used in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] [[roleplaying game]] ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'' supplement ''[[Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi]]''.<ref name="GG5:RotJ">''[[Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi]]''</ref> The name was then [[canon]]ized with its inclusion in [[James Luceno]]'s [[2014]] novel [[Tarkin (novel)|''Tarkin'']].<ref name="Trkn" />

Blista-Vanee's costume was designed by [[Nilo Rodis-Jamero]]. Rodis-Jamero felt that the look of the Imperial advisors was one of the most exciting designs from ''Return of the Jedi'' and thought their design would need to convey an idea about the kind of world that the Emperor lived in. Rodis-Jamero based the look on that of [[Wikipedia:Catholic Church|Catholic]] [[Wikipedia:Bishop|bishops]], with red coloring and ornate headpieces.<ref name="Annotated" />
